Redeem iCoke Gift Box Voucher was a quest used as a promotion for iCoke only in Taiwan region. Another quest with a similar name was managed to be obtained by players in other regions of the world, though it couldn't have been completed. It was being shared in battlegrounds in order to spread it. As a result, this quest along with the others was removed entirely from the game with patch 5.2.0.

:Not to be confused with Red Cloud Mesa, called "Redrock Mesa" in early development. Redrock Mesa is a region of cliffs and winding paths that sprawls across southeastern Vol'dun, covering the area between the Valley of Sorrows to the north, Zul'Ahjin to the northwest, the Ashvane Encampment to the southwest, and the Eternal Spring and Temple of Akunda to the south. The mesa is dominated by a small peak inhabited by pterrordax, though it also extends south to a small plateau immediately next to the Temple of Akunda, where ranishu swarm in and around Redrock Cavern.

The Red Hand was a group of assassins who exercised their unlawful ways in Drustvar, in Kul Tiras. Their most famous hit was a job given by the matriarch of House Waycrest, Meredith Waycrest, who having a dislike for her daughter's fiance, Alexander Treadward, ordered the gang to strike him down during their wedding ceremony. Their leader, Roland the Knife, would take the man's life, but in the commotion, he too would die and be left to rot in the basement of Whitegrove Chapel. Following the death of their leader, the Red Hand seemingly disappeared from Drustvar. Nothing remains of their presence, aside from the contract Lady Meredith signed, whose sole owner lies dead where he stood.
Red Hand Assassins were humans located in Whitegrove Chapel in Drustvar.

Redemption for the Redeemer is the traditional post-final-boss quest, this time for defeating Sire Denathrius in Castle Nathria. Completing the quest triggers a cutscene showing Denathrius' fate, but only if the player has also completed Sanguine Depths: An Ally Within. Completing this quest actually a required part of the overarching Shadowlands campaign. In addition to completing this quest, players must have also completed The Captive King in Oribos to be offered the next quest, An Echo in the Darkness.

Redelav Tower is the home of The Countess found within the Eternal Terrace. It is permanently locked from the outside, and its interior is only accessible to the adventurer through the private mirror given to Duke Theotar from his estate, Thornhill Manor, in the Old Gate.

The Redelav District is the part of the Castle Ward where all the venthyr nobility's estates are located, with the exception of Thornhill Manor. The Menagerie of the Master is located to the north, the Old Gate to the east, and the Chalice District to the south. Curiously, it does not connect to the Eternal Terrace. It shares a namesake with Redelav Hall and The Countess's Redelav Tower in the Eternal Terrace, but it is unclear why. Members of House Briarbane are seen patrolling the road with two Stone Legion stoneborn; House Briarbane is also known to control other venthyr through their sinstone. A member of House Primrose is seen in Sinfall, but they are subject to having their stone fiend
Redelav Hall is the residence of House Redelav, located in the Redelav District.

Redeemed Souls are lost souls saved from the Maw by the Maw Walker and are returned to their Covenant's sanctum. The souls are used in addition to Reservoir Anima to research and unlock upgrades to their sanctum. Players will gain five souls a week until they reach Renown (Shadowlands) levels 15, 24, and 32, which upgrades their Soulkeeper, allowing them to gather 10, 15, or 20 souls per week instead, respectively.

__NOTOC__ Refined Deeprock Salt was a kind of Salt processed from Deeprock Salt using a Salt Shaker made by Engineers. It was NOT a Leatherworking pattern, although only Leatherworkers with skill level of 250 or higher could use Salt Shaker. It used to have a cooldown time of three days. Similar to the Philosopher's Stone transmutations, having more salt shakers didn't speed the process. It was re-added to the game and only sold by Far'kul Flametongue during the Kosh'harg.

Regrowth is a druid healing spell. Regrowth is a fast spell to cast and heals for a decent amount, but this is balanced by poor mana efficiency. While the spell has a small HoT component it is mainly a direct heal.

Refuge Pointe is a base of the kingdom of Stromgarde. When the Stromgarde capital was in ruins following the Third War, most of the populace fled south, while the proud remnants of Stromgarde's elite army stayed behind, determined to fight on to reclaim their land. It is from Refuge Pointe that the Alliance's military operations in the area are conducted, most of which is concerned with aiding the Stromgarde army retake their former capital and securing resources for the Alliance in the Arathi Highlands. There is also an Alliance entrance to the Arathi Basin. It is more of an outpost than a full town since it has only tents and no mailbox. The inn is the southernmost tent.

Reggifuz is a goblin stable master located in Ratchet of Northern Barrens. He is found outside of the Broken Keel Tavern in that town. He carries a walking stick.

Regthar Deathgate is an orc quest giver located in a small fortified camp by the road west of the Crossroads, in the Northern Barrens. The camp is made up of a burrow and a pig farm, with Lanti'gah walking around. Regthar is in charge of the Horde operations against the centaur all over the Northern Barrens. He sent scouts such as Ta'jari to all the oases of the area. During the Legion Invasions, Regthar defended the burrow against the invading demons.
Reef Crawlers are crabs native to Darkshore prior to the Cataclysm. They were often hunted for their fine crab meat along with Encrusted Tide Crawlers.
Reef Frenzies are frenzies found all along the western coastline of Silverpine Forest. They can be skinned for Shiny Fish Scales, and they drop Soft Frenzy Flesh for cooking.

Reef Sharks are sharks found off the coasts of Westfall, Ashenvale and Silverpine Forest. Their appearance varies between normal sharks and hammerhead sharks. They can be skinned for Light Leather, Ruined Leather Scraps, or Light Hide.

The Regional Defenders was the local defense force of footmen for the unnamed village in the King's Road within Alterac during the time of the Third War. When they were besieged by the Undead Scourge, despite their best efforts they were unable to save the villagers. Forced to retreat and hounded by the undead, the small defense force led by an sergeant would be reinforced by the arrival of Prince Arthas and his forces. Few in number, the Regional Defenders joined Prince Arthas's forces. They were also stationed in Andorhal but were overrun by the Scourge.

The Refugee Leadership (or simply Human Leaders) were the humans that commanded the refugees from Hillsbrad Foothills when the Forsaken invaded it. They took control of Fenris Isle and its keep. A number of refugees on the isle were killed by the Forsaken adventurer and raised by the val'kyr Agatha as Forsaken. The duo then entered the keep only to find the leadership allying with the Gilneas Liberation Front and becoming worgen so that the Forsaken wouldn't be able to raise them into undeath. The refugee survivors, now worgen, eventually fought against the Forsaken and their orcish allies in the mainland of Silverpine Forest, with Caretaker Smithers attempting to ambush the adventurer, but

When you die you are prompted with a dialog box to Release Spirit, which turns you into a ghost (or wisp spirit) at the nearest graveyard. If resurrection is unavailable, releasing your spirit and finding your corpse (or talking to the Spirit Healer, at a penalty) is the only way to come back to life. If you don't click the button within 6 minutes, you will automatically release at the nearest graveyard.

Reins of the Winterspring Frostsaber summons a unique frostsaber mount that is not wearing any armor. It is the only (Alliance) epic mount that can be used with the novice riding skill; however, players must still be level 40 to use the mount.

One central issue of many Loot systems (Fixed price systems in particular) is that they provide disproportionate rewards to people who are able to raid more often. This means that if someone raids maybe half as frequently as more hardcore raid members competing for the same gear, that less-often raider will never be able to get highend gear until the hardcore players have all they want. For some raids this effect is OK (because regular members are crucial to progress), other raids may feel that the ratio of gear to effort should be the same, no matter whether somebody raids 3x/week or 1x/month.
